_doc: The fish photos re-judged for phases on the cited phase list tools/fish_phases.json (REE-52; docs/decisions/2026-11-21-fish-phase-flag-from-cited-list.md). batches: {batch: {date, reading, read: {photo: tag or null}}}: every photo read, with the phase written in its judging file, or null (read, no tag: the quote does not let the photo show it). A batch with written false (and its note) was read but its tags were not written to the judging files: the tags are as read. untagged: {species id: why its photos get no tag from a tile}. A photo not listed was not read.

untagged.s032: Genicanthus lamarck: the quote names no colours ("different colors in mature adults only")
untagged.s073: Amphiprion frenatus: the quote names no colours ("always different colors between mature adults")
untagged.s223: Epibulus brevis: the quote's differences (a drab male; females of varied colours) do not tell one photo
untagged.s224: Hemigymnus melapterus: the sexes differ in the scale margins of the dark rear body (black-rimmed with a green line, or pale blue-green and black), too fine for a tile
untagged.s225: Hemigymnus fasciatus: males "similar in colour to females"; their marks (bars often tinged green, spots behind the eye and on the nape) are not constant or too fine for a tile
untagged.s232: Halichoeres chrysus: the dorsal-fin spots that tell the sexes (one, two or three) are too small for a tile, and hidden on a folded fin
untagged.s243: Halichoeres nebulosus: the male's pink band below the eye is too small for a tile, and the quote describes no female
untagged.s255: Thalassoma hardwicke: "color pattern remains similar with growth", terminal males only brighter
untagged.s256: Thalassoma lunare: terminal males "similar but more blue overall", a difference of degree
untagged.s265: Bodianus dictynna: the terminal male's black spots on the dorsal, anal and pelvic fins cannot be told from a tile (small, on folded fins), and the quote describes no other phase
untagged.s307: Parapercis clathrata: the mark (a white-edged black spot above the gill opening) is too small for a tile
untagged.s351: Cantherhines dumerili: the male's orange peduncle spines are too small for a tile; a "deeper orange" tail is a difference of degree
untagged.s468: Caranx ignobilis: the quote names no colours ("always different colors between mature adults")
untagged.s580: Parapercis pacifica: the marks (3-4 versus 6-7 ocelli on the lower body, the male's cheek marks) are too fine for a tile
untagged.s607: Iniistius pentadactylus: the photos with the female's white patch with red scale margins also show a row of small spots along the lateral line, which the quote says females lack (seen at 1024 px): the quote's two marks conflict
untagged.s654: Vanderhorstia dorsomacula: the differences (yellow spots or streaks, irregular dark spots on the first dorsal fin) are too fine for a tile
